prs.body:
Bug: a sponsored VaultWithdraw to a distinct destination could fail with tecINVARIANT_FAILED. ValidVault only added the transaction fee back onto the sender's XRP delta when the sender itself paid it. When a co-signed sponsor pays the fee instead, the sender's AccountRoot is still touched (sequence processing) but its balance doesn't change, leaving a present but economically zero delta. Combined with the destination's positive delta, the invariant saw two apparent recipients and rejected the withdrawal.

Fix: ValidVault resolves the actual fee payer via Transactor::getFeePayer (sender, delegate, co-signed sponsor, or pre-funded sponsorship), adds the fee back only onto whichever AccountRoot actually paid it, and collapses the resulting zero delta to absence instead of leaving it in place. The payout recipient is now picked explicitly from sfDestination/sfAccount instead of being inferred from which side happens to carry a delta. Gated behind fixCleanup3_4_0 since this changes consensus behavior.

Added regression tests in VaultBugs_test.cpp covering the sponsored third-party withdrawal and a sponsor named as its own withdrawal destination, each asserting tecINVARIANT_FAILED before the amendment and tesSUCCESS after.

reviewCommentsList.body: Yea, `decreaseOwnerCountForObject` looks up the object's reserve sponsor and passes it along to `adjustOwnerCountSigned`. That function only accepts a non-null sponsor when the count-holder (the SLE whose count is being adjusted) is `ltACCOUNT_ROOT`:  for any other type it returns without decrementing anything. Here the count-holder is the broker, which is `ltLOAN_BROKER`, not `ltACCOUNT_ROOT`. So if loans ever became sponsorable, passing that sponsor through would make the broker's outstanding-loan count stop decrementing on delete, instead of raising an error;

reviewCommentsList.author: Copilot
reviewCommentsList.body: Changing `Sponsor` from `Supported::No` to `Supported::Yes` makes the server treat the amendment as *supported* (it will be included in `detail::supportedAmendments()` and the `AmendmentTable` constructed in `Application.cpp`). Per `Feature.h`'s documented process, `Supported::Yes` should only be used once development is complete and the server is intended to remain compatible if the amendment becomes enabled on-network; if the goal is only “easier testing”, this change is risky to merge into mainline.

reviewCommentsList.author: Copilot
reviewCommentsList.body: PR description says "API Impact N/A", but this is a change in an installed public header (`include/xrpl/...`) that changes the compiled-in supported-amendments set; that’s externally observable for downstream consumers and has protocol/network compatibility implications. Please update the PR description to reflect the impact (or clarify why it’s considered N/A).

reviewCommentsList.author: xrplf-ai-reviewer[bot]
reviewCommentsList.body:
`Supported::Yes` is irreversible once shipped — confirm `Sponsor` is implementation-complete, not just easier to test.

The MR description says "for easier testing", which implies the feature isn't production-ready. Per `Feature.h:37-40`, once `Supported::Yes` ships in a release it can **never** be safely reverted to `Supported::No` without risking amendment-blocking all nodes on that release. If this is still in development, use a local or devnet build instead.

```suggestion
XRPL_FEATURE(Sponsor,                     Supported::No,  VoteBehavior::DefaultNo)
```
